subject.title: fix: treat trusted-proxy gateway auth as doctor auth proof

question: Should exposed Gateway doctor output downgrade from critical to warning only when trusted-proxy configuration satisfies the same usable-auth boundary that Gateway runtime accepts?
rationale: The mechanical repair is clear, but changing an exposed-Gateway diagnostic severity is a security-policy decision that code review cannot make on behalf of the feature owners.

options.title: Require runtime-aligned proof
options.body: Repair the doctor predicate so only complete, runtime-valid trusted-proxy configurations receive warning-level exposure guidance, then accept the severity downgrade for that narrow case.

options.title: Keep all trusted-proxy exposure critical
options.body: Retain the current critical diagnostic for exposed trusted-proxy deployments and limit any change to clearer remediation wording.

options.title: Accept mode-only warning classification
options.body: Allow all trusted-proxy modes to receive warning output despite invalid runtime configurations, knowingly leaving doctor less strict than startup.

recommendation.title: Require runtime-aligned proof
recommendation.body: Repair the doctor predicate so only complete, runtime-valid trusted-proxy configurations receive warning-level exposure guidance, then accept the severity downgrade for that narrow case.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the trusted-proxy auth contract and are the strongest available routing candidate for its diagnostic security boundary.
